method: Forced fit of the SPHEREx empirical PSF (EPSF extension, nearest entry on the detector) at the catalogue position moved to each exposure (proper motion, parallax), flux free, constant background, Gaia DR3 field stars and catalogue neighbours fitted at fixed positions; 11x11 native-pixel stamp of IMAGE - ZODI, FLAGS-masked pixels left out, weights from VARIANCE. Flux = MJy/sr x pixel solid angle at the target (WCS) -> uJy (total flux of the normalised EPSF). Errors from VARIANCE x noise_scale (robust S/N scatter of the same fit at 24 random positions, per season and detector, >= 1). Wavelength and bandwidth at the target pixel from the spectral WCS (WCS-WAVE). Saturated cores: PSF fitted to the unsaturated wing pixels only (saturated_wing, a rough estimate).

status_labels.flagged: flagged (bad pixels or source off its predicted position; not binned)

caveats: Flux check: two unsaturated Gaia field stars (eps_indi_b cutouts) agree with 2MASS J/H/Ks and AllWISE W1/W2 to 0.93-1.06 (mean ratio 1.00).

Saturated points (saturated_wing) come from the PSF wings only. On unsaturated stars with the core masked, the estimate recovers 0.88 +- 0.12 of the flux for a 1.5 px core and 0.60 +- 0.19 for a 2 px core; larger saturated cores can be off by a factor of 2. They are never plotted as normal points.
Each exposure sees the source through a narrow band (bandwidth_um) at one time: a variable source mixes time and wavelength within a season.
